primary_claim: A new Self-Boundary Consistency evaluation, tested on three small open-weight models (Phi-3-Mini-4k, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, TinyLlama-1.1B), differentiates models that look similar on conventional benchmarks: Qwen2.5-3B scored highest on self-boundary consistency (avg 0.683) with the lowest semantic drift, while Phi-3-Mini and TinyLlama scored lower (avg 0.557 and 0.570) and drifted far more often.

effect.value: Model A (Phi-3-Mini)=0.557, Model B (Qwen2.5-3B)=0.683, Model C (TinyLlama)=0.570

stated_future_work: apply the rubric to larger models and agentic systems to test how well the framework scales and whether the same failure modes appear across different model classes
explore the relationship between behavioural consistency and underlying mechanisms, e.g. whether representation drift or activation-level instabilities correlate with boundary-failure patterns
expand the dataset families, deepen the scoring regimes, or introduce additional sub-measures
limitations_stated: this is a first cut, very basic evaluation
test runs used small open-weight models on cheap Colab GPU compute and were not intended to benchmark model quality
quote: these results show that the evaluation differentiates between models that appear similar on conventional benchmarks
